bullets.title: NVDA premarket gains on Hon Hai beat; AI hardware demand confirmed
bullets.body: NVDA led Mag 7 gains premarket (+1.2%) after supplier Foxconn/Hon Hai reported 54.2% YoY revenue growth to $29.4B and net income of $1.9B vs. $1.8B expected. Analysts view the beat as confirming robust global demand for AI hardware.

bullets.title: NVDA product shift from memory to optics; NVL576 adoption driving MRVL, SMCI upside
bullets.body: Fintwit notes NVDA is pivoting content from memories to optics, with higher NVL576 adoption expected in 2027. The optical interconnect opportunity is seen as a secondary benefit for semiconductor suppliers MRVL and SMCI.

bullets.title: Semiconductor pullback bottom thesis gains traction; SOX at 27x fwd P/E
bullets.body: Multiple accounts argue the worst of the semis pullback may be behind us, citing SOX valuations correcting to 27x forward P/E, cleaner positioning, and improving sentiment. One analyst notes the tech index is transitioning from 'unwind & consolidation' toward a longer rebound that could exceed consensus duration.

bullets.title: SMCI surges ~8% premarket; JPMorgan raises PT to $45 from $32
bullets.body: SMCI gained approximately 8% premarket on strong earnings results alongside CRWV's results. JPMorgan responded by raising its SMCI price target to $45 from $32.

bullets.title: NBIS Q2 beats across the board: EPS -$0.68 vs. -$0.86 est.; revenue +454% YoY
bullets.body: Nebius reported Q2 EPS of -$0.68 (beating -$0.86 estimate) and revenue of $582.3M (vs. $573.9M expected), up 454% YoY. New contracts reportedly priced at >$40M/MW. Earnings release was delayed and contained a typo, drawing some negative commentary on execution.

bullets.title: CRWV surges 16-18% premarket on clean quarter; multiple PT raises
bullets.body: CoreWeave posted strong results with revenue roughly doubling on accelerating AI infrastructure demand, sending the stock up 16-18% premarket. JPMorgan raised its PT to $120 (from $110, Neutral), Mizuho to $115 (from $100, Neutral), and Piper Sandler also raised its target.

bullets.title: LITE results described as 'incredibly bullish' on strong laser demand
bullets.body: Lumentum's results were characterized as 'incredibly bullish' by fintwit accounts, citing strong laser demand; SIVE gained 7% on spillover from LITE's positive print.

bullets.title: AMD: server CPU TAM to surpass $200B by 2030; Radeon RX 9000 GPU prices up 20%
bullets.body: AMD stated it expects the server CPU market to exceed $200B by 2030 in a significant TAM expansion signal. Separately, AMD officially raised Radeon RX 9000 GPU prices by up to 20%, with the RX 9070 XT now exceeding $1,000—a potential margin tailwind or demand risk.

bullets.title: Wall Street tightly clustered on July CPI: core 0.16-0.20% M/M; headline 3.30-3.40% Y/Y
bullets.body: Major banks forecast July core CPI at 0.16-0.20% M/M and 2.4-2.5% Y/Y; headline at 0.0-0.10% M/M and 3.30-3.40% Y/Y. The narrow consensus range raises the risk of outsized market moves on any miss. One account flagged that CPI data may have been leaked ahead of the release.

bullets.title: Market waiting for Jackson Hole; CPI seen as unlikely catalyst for volatility
bullets.body: Fintwit sentiment suggests markets have 'decided nothing matters until maybe Jackson Hole,' with CPI seen as unlikely to trigger significant volatility. Fed front-runner signals are reportedly dovish ahead of the print, partly supporting gold's rise.

bullets.title: CTAs hold record short bond positions; ~$300M P&L sensitivity per 1bp in 10Y yield
bullets.body: Per UBS, CTAs tripled their underweight/short positions in global bonds to record levels, with approximately $300M P&L impact per 1 basis point move in 10-year Treasury yields. Similar positioning is visible in TLT fixed strike volatility.

bullets.title: Goldman derivatives trader warns AI trade momentum may be stalling
bullets.body: A Goldman Sachs top derivatives trader flagged that market sentiment has shifted from 'fear of the Fed to complacency' and that AI trade momentum may be stalling—a structural caution for the sector even as individual names like NVDA and CRWV print strong results.

bullets.title: Norway's $2.3T wealth fund posts record $184.3B H1 profit, driven by Asian tech
bullets.body: Norges Bank's sovereign wealth fund earned a record $184.3B in first-half profits, with Asian technology stocks as the primary driver. The fund also separately disclosed a 7.3M Class A share stake in SpaceX via SEC filing.

bullets.title: US-Iran ceasefire stalled; crude erases losses on no-extension headline
bullets.body: A senior Iranian source told Reuters there are no discussions on extending the ceasefire, claiming the U.S. violated the interim pact within 48 hours of reaching it. Brent and WTI crude futures erased earlier losses on the headline. Pakistan separately indicated the MOU deadline could be extended.

bullets.title: BOJ September rate hike odds rise to 79%; USD/JPY and global rates divergence
bullets.body: OIS markets are pricing a 79% probability of a BOJ rate hike in September, up from 66% on Monday—bullish for the yen. Simultaneously, UST 10yr yields fell 2bps while JGB 10yr rose 4bps, widening the rate divergence.

bullets.title: S&P 500 earnings acceleration: +51% YoY EPS growth from 448 reporters
bullets.body: With 448 S&P 500 companies having reported, year-over-year EPS acceleration stands at +51%—described as 'epic' and well ahead of bearish consensus expectations. SPY volume decelerated during the recent 2-day correction while RSP hit all-time highs, suggesting broad market health.

bullets.title: Consumer credit stress signals: 12.9% of credit card balances 90+ days delinquent
bullets.body: 12.9% of US credit card balances are 90+ days delinquent—near the highest level since 2011—with serious delinquency highest among 18-29 year-olds per NY Fed 2Q26 data. Total household debt balances declined marginally in the quarter.

bullets.title: Labor market softening: private payrolls sub-10K for 7 straight weeks; hiring plans at Oct 2022 high
bullets.body: ADP data shows private payrolls came in under 10K for the four weeks ending July 25—the seventh consecutive week of slowing hiring. Contrasting that, NFIB July hiring plans rose to their highest level since October 2022, though unfilled job openings remain elevated.

bullets.title: INTC Razor Lake-AX halo SoC confirmed in HWiNFO, targeting AMD competition circa 2028
bullets.body: Intel's Razor Lake-AX halo-class SoC has surfaced in HWiNFO support files, confirming development of a product designed to compete directly with AMD's top-end offering, with an expected launch around 2028.

bullets.title: Hindenburg Omen triggers 13 times in 3 months for SPX—historically rare warning
bullets.body: The Hindenburg Omen has been triggered 13 times in the past 3 months for the S&P 500—only the third time in history with that many triggers in a 3-month window. Prior instances with similar clustering preceded the 1987 and 2008 crashes, though signal reliability is debated.
